subject: Workplace Skills
title: The Hybrid Meeting Problem
description: A quick, practical guide to The Hybrid Meeting Problem.

hook.text: Five people in a conference room and three on a screen. The remote three couldn't hear half the discussion.

buildup.text: Hybrid meetings almost always favor the in-room participants. Side conversations exclude remote attendees.

discovery.text: The fix: if one person is remote, everyone joins from their own screen. Equal setup means equal experience.

twist.text: This feels wasteful when people are in the same building, but it's the only way to keep remote colleagues equal.

climax.text: If everyone-on-screen isn't possible, assign one in-room ally to relay chat and surface remote hands.

punchline.text: One remote? Everyone on screen. Equal access matters.

quiz.question: What's the best solution for hybrid meetings with remote attendees?
options: Put a larger screen in the conference room
Have everyone join from individual screens to equalize the experience
Let remote workers dial in by phone instead
